full_judgment: 6. On the other hand, Mr M Khaled Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties, strongly submits that the trial Court has rightly and correctly granted temporary injunction in consideration of the registered deed of the predecessor of the plaintiff finding a prima facie possession balance of convenience and inconvenience in favour of the plaintiff and irreparable loss in absence of such order, etc. He contends that registration of a document itself has presumptive value of execution of the deed and the appellate Court below affirmed the finding of the trial Court as last Court of facts in consideration of the registered deed of the predecessor of the plaintiff including their own registered kabala finding prima facie possession balance of convenience and inconvenience in favour of the plaintiff and has committed no error of law and this Court should not disturb the finding of the last Court of facts in this revisional jurisdiction, etc. In support of his submission Mr Ahmed cited decisions in the case of Md Nurul Hoque Khan vs Bangladesh Bank reported in 39 DLR 310, Abani Mohan Saha vs Assistant Custodian (SDO) Vested Property Chandpur reported in 39 DLR (AD) 223 and in the case of Rupban Bibi vs Aynul Kha reported in 44 DLR (AD) 144.
